why: Market-basket analysis drives cross-selling, store layout and "frequently bought together" recommendations in retail and e-commerce.
explain: A rule looks like **{bread} → {butter}**: customers who buy bread also buy butter.
**Support** = how often the itemset appears in all baskets. **Confidence** = P(butter | bread). **Lift** = confidence ÷ P(butter): how much more likely butter is when bread is bought than in general.
**Lift > 1** means a real positive association; lift ≈ 1 means independence; lift < 1 means the items substitute for each other.
**Apriori** speeds up the search: if an itemset is rare, every bigger itemset containing it is rare too, so it can be pruned. FP-Growth is a faster alternative.

formula.plain: How much buying A raises the chance of buying B, compared with B's normal rate.

example.title: Scoring three rules on the ten bills
steps: Ten grocery bills: bread in 7, milk in 6, butter in 4, tea in 3, biscuits in 2
{butter} → {bread}: all 4 butter bills contain bread → support 0.4, confidence 1.0, lift = 1.0 / 0.7 ≈ 1.43
{tea} → {biscuits}: both in 2 of the 3 tea bills → support 0.2, confidence ≈ 0.67, lift = 0.67 / 0.2 ≈ 3.33
{milk} → {bread}: both in 4 of the 6 milk bills → support 0.4, confidence ≈ 0.67, lift = 0.67 / 0.7 ≈ 0.95
example.result: Milk → bread has the same confidence as tea → biscuits, but lift below 1: it is popularity, not association. Tea → biscuits is the strongest real link, even though it is rarer. Test a tea-and-biscuits offer.

mistakes: Ranking rules by confidence alone (popular items get high confidence by default; check lift).
Mining with a very low support threshold (thousands of meaningless rules).
takeaways: Support = frequency, confidence = conditional probability, lift = association strength
avoid: Personalised recommendations at scale (use collaborative filtering)

practice.code:
# pip install mlxtend  (run locally)
import pandas as pd
from mlxtend.preprocessing import TransactionEncoder
from mlxtend.frequent_patterns import apriori, association_rules
bills = [["bread", "butter", "milk"], ["bread", "butter"], ["bread", "jam"], ["milk", "tea"], ["bread", "butter", "jam"],
         ["milk", "bread"], ["tea", "biscuits"], ["bread", "butter", "milk"], ["milk", "tea", "biscuits"], ["bread", "milk"]]
te = TransactionEncoder()
baskets = pd.DataFrame(te.fit(bills).transform(bills), columns=te.columns_)
fi = apriori(baskets, min_support=0.2, use_colnames=True)
rules = association_rules(fi, metric="lift", min_threshold=0)
cols = ["antecedents", "consequents", "support", "confidence", "lift"]
print(rules.sort_values("lift", ascending=False)[cols].round(2).head(4).to_string())   # tea → biscuits: lift 3.33

options: Slightly less likely to be bought together than by chance

check.q: A in 100 baskets, B in 50, both in 20, out of 500. Confidence(A → B)?
